sample_unit: guideline-derived clinical scenarios (each queried once for clinicians and once for patients)

links.outcome: Readability of patient-facing LLM outputs versus requested ≤6th-grade reading level
links.effect: Mean SMOG 10.4±1.1, FKGL 6.9±0.7, FRE 72.4±5.3; about 7th-grade level, slightly above AMA recommendations despite a ≤6th-grade prompt.
links.quote: Readability analyses outputted a mean SMOG of 10.4±1.1, FKGL 6.9±0.7, and FRE 72.4±5.3, indicating readability at a ∼7th-grade level, but within "fairly easy" comprehension.

links.outcome: Accuracy and plain-language readability of patient-facing AI outputs
links.effect: Patient-facing accuracy mean 2.33±0.72 (range 1-3) versus clinician 2.93±0.26; key details such as mJOA thresholds omitted; readability about 7th-grade level.
links.quote: Patient-facing responses were less consistent (mean 2.33±0.72; range: 1-3) with no full inter-rater agreement.

links.outcome: Accuracy of LLM outputs against guideline reference standard, graded by 3 spine surgeons
links.effect: Clinician-facing outputs mean 2.93±0.26 with no inaccurate outputs; patient-facing mean 2.33±0.72 with omissions of key details.
links.quote: Clinician-facing outputs were highly accurate (mean 2.93±0.26) with near-perfect agreement and no outputs graded as inaccurate.

links.outcome: Clinical accuracy of generative AI responses when written for a lay, low-reading-level user
links.effect: Patient-facing accuracy fell to mean 2.33±0.72 versus 2.93±0.26 for clinician-facing; lower scores reflected omission of mJOA thresholds and surgical versus conservative care distinctions.
links.quote: Lower scores reflected omission of key details such as mJOA thresholds and clear distinctions between surgical and conservative care.

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM translation of clinical guidelines for clinicians vs patients with a prompt constraint specifying a <=6th-grade reading level, and measures readability and accuracy outcomes.
